cohort: Pregnant women ≤ 19 years of age (n = 104) compared to non-adolescent women (n = 414) in Sao Tome and Principe
finding: Adolescent pregnancies were associated with worse perinatal outcomes, including fetal distress and a higher need for neonatal resuscitation maneuvers.
mod_finding: While adolescent mothers had a threefold higher risk of obstructed labor, this finding was not statistically significant, and mode of delivery was similar between the groups.
